previous_description: A named registry for reusable API definition objects (schemas, responses, parameters, examples, requestBodies, headers, securitySchemes, links, callbacks) that enables $ref referencing throughout the specification. Component entries are not rendered directly — they must be referenced by operations, parameters, or schemas to take effect. Component name keys must match the pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9.\-_]+$ per OpenAPI 3.0 — arbitrary strings are not valid component identifiers.
definition: The single container object within an OpenAPI document that holds named, reusable definitions (schemas, responses, parameters, examples, request bodies, headers, security schemes, links and callbacks), each addressable by a '#/components/<kind>/<name>' $ref pointer. It defines no paths or operations itself; its entries take effect only when referenced.

distinguish_from.when: the element is the root object carrying openapi, info, paths and servers, of which the components section is only one child.
the element is an individual data-shape definition, whether inline or stored under components.schemas, rather than the registry that holds it.
the element is an operation's map of HTTP status codes to Response objects, not the components.responses registry of named reusable responses.
the element maps URL path templates to PathItem objects that define live API surface, rather than holding unreferenced reusable definitions.

code_evidence: A top-level 'components:' key in an openapi.yaml/openapi.json with sub-maps such as schemas, securitySchemes, parameters or responses
JSON Reference strings of the form "$ref: '#/components/schemas/User'" or '#/components/responses/NotFound' elsewhere in the spec

Programmatic spec builders populating the section, e.g. springdoc 'new OpenAPI().components(new Components().addSecuritySchemes(...))', NestJS DocumentBuilder().addBearerAuth(), or drf-spectacular/FastAPI registering models under components.schemas
notes: The composes→api.paths edge is invalid: an OpenAPI 3.0 Components object has no paths or pathItems, which exist only in 3.1. components.responses holds Response objects, not a Responses map, so drop composes→api.responses. api.response appears under both aggregates and composes; pick one. The oauthflows→components association is spurious, because flows nest in securityscheme.
